title: Can you use static methods in an interface, how are they called, and are they inherited by implementing classes?
shortTitle: How are static methods in interfaces called?
keyPoints: Interface static methods are called ONLY via InterfaceName.method(), never via an implementing class or instance.
Static methods are NOT inherited: implementing classes cannot call them using their own class name.
Static methods CANNOT be overridden: a class can define a method with the same name, but it is a separate method.
They replace the companion utility class pattern: Comparator.comparing() instead of ComparatorUtils.
Common uses: factory methods (List.of), utility functions (Predicate.not), and constants (Taxable.gstRate).
They keep related functionality together with the interface instead of scattering it across utility classes.
Java 9+ expanded this pattern: List.of(), Set.of(), Map.of() are all static methods on collection interfaces.

s1_definition.oneliner: Interface static methods are called via InterfaceName.method() only, are not inherited by implementing classes, cannot be overridden, and replace companion utility classes.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Calling**: static methods on interfaces are called exclusively via `InterfaceName.method()`, never via an implementing class or an instance reference.
- **Not inherited**: if `AccountService` has a static method, `SavingsAccountServiceImpl.method()` does not compile.
- **Not overridable**: a class can define a method with the same name, but it is a completely separate method, not an override.
- **Replaces utility classes**: instead of `Collections.sort()` (utility class) and `Collection` (interface), Java 8 puts `Comparator.comparing()` and `Predicate.not()` directly on the interface.
- **Factory methods**: `List.of()`, `Map.of()`, `Set.of()` (Java 9) are static methods on collection interfaces.
- **Keeps logic together**: related functionality lives on the interface instead of being scattered across utility classes.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) publishing a standard interest calculator on their website. Every bank in India can use the RBI calculator by visiting rbi.gov.in/calculator (InterfaceName.method()). But no bank can put that calculator on their own website and claim it as theirs (not inherited). HDFC cannot say HDFC.calculateInterest(); it must say RBI.calculateInterest(). The calculator belongs to RBI (the interface), not to any specific bank (implementing class).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Static method on interface:
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ interface InterestService {   │
  │   static roundToPaisa(amt)   │ ← belongs HERE
  │ }                             │
  └──────────────────────────────┘
         │
         │  InterestService.roundToPaisa()  ← CORRECT
         │
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ class FDService              │
  │   implements InterestService │
  │                              │
  │   FDService.roundToPaisa()   │ ← COMPILE ERROR!
  │   (NOT inherited)            │
  └──────────────────────────────┘

  Before Java 8:           After Java 8:
  Collections.sort(list)   list.sort(cmp)         (default)
  ComparatorUtils.by(fn)   Comparator.comparing() (static)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Interface static methods are called exclusively via InterfaceName.method() and are not inherited by implementing classes. They cannot be overridden. If a class defines a method with the same name, it is a completely separate method, not an override. This is fundamentally different from default methods, which are inherited and can be overridden.

The practical impact is seen across the Java standard library. List.of(), Map.of(), and Set.of() replace Collections.unmodifiableList(). Comparator.comparing() and Comparator.naturalOrder() replace manual Comparator instantiation. Predicate.not() replaces verbose negation lambdas. The pattern keeps related functionality together on the interface itself rather than scattering it across utility classes.

In Rajesh's interest calculation service at National Bank of India, the InterestService interface has one abstract method (calculate) and two static methods (roundToPaisa and simpleInterest). Both are called via InterestService.methodName() by all implementing classes. Before Java 8, these would have been in a separate InterestUtils class.

Remember one sentence: interface static methods are called via InterfaceName.method(), are not inherited, cannot be overridden, and replace companion utility classes.
